4 of 11 assumptions changed in version 3
  • WPL-U1A new version means you have something new to see. Fixes keep the number. (your "version 3, version 4")
  • WPL-U2Old versions open from the version switcher at the top of the sidebar. (changed in v3)
  • WPL-U3One task code, one document, one link. Several issues or PRs stay in one document. (your "same document all across")
  • WPL-U4Your answers still go to the code ledger and memory. The document shows them. (memory rules, 19 Oct)
  • WPL-U5Feedwrk documents live in ~/Projects/feedwrk/docs/work/, others in ~/firstmate/data/work/. A main-account Haiku publishes for second-account workers. Feedwrk documents are shared with Kaspars by link. (your WPL-D5 answer)
  • WPL-U6Feedwrk documents use Feedwrk Docs from the design hub, through the skill. Never feedwrk-doc.css, feedwrk-doc.js or the feedwrk-docs skill. (changed in v3)
  • WPL-U7The PR and tester parts of Verification are written by a small main-account worker per event, not a new program. (simplest path first)
  • WPL-U8Parked work keeps its document with a Paused status. TikTok and Pinterest stays parked until you say. (your 14 Oct priorities)
  • WPL-U9Every new version's Overview opens with "What changed in version N", each line linked to the page it changed. (v2)
  • WPL-U10The issue body is yours. Firstmate rewrites its document parts when the design changes. Build runs never edit it. (issue-handoff rule 6)
  • WPL-U11A document for another project uses that project's design system. Firstmate documents, which have none, use Feedwrk Docs. (changed in v3)
6 risks to watch
  • WPL-R1Records that had to be fed went stale three times before. Here the document is the record, and each update follows an event firstmate already handles.
  • WPL-R2Document, issue and code ledger drift apart. The check before every "ready" link compares them.
  • WPL-R3Two workers write one document at once. One writer per document, and a publish over a newer version is refused.
  • WPL-R4Tester results are per step, not per check, until steps carry the check codes (WPL-A6).
  • WPL-R5The published verification map is the 8 Oct snapshot (229 checks). The live map has 234 checks and 9 gaps.
  • WPL-R6The Feedwrk workspace instructions still tell workers to use feedwrk-docs.

Detail 4 findings

Old versions

Republishing keeps the link and gives each publish a version id. Reading returns only the newest version, an old id in the link is ignored, and the publish label cannot be read back.

Earlier attempts

The 2 Oct document system was a separate repository and command line that had to be fed. Its last commit is from 2 Oct. The status board and the Captain's Deck went the same way.

What an issue must hold

The issue-handoff skill lists nine checks, R1 to R9, that a build issue must pass. The body is yours, and build runs never edit it. No issue or PR template exists in feedwrk-backend or modern-ux-shine.

Tests and checks

Tester steps have their own ids and land in results.json per step. The verification map has its own codes in checks.json. Neither is tied to a design's check list.

How many pages

71 worker reports in firstmate's data cite 86 different pages, and about 256 page ids appear across all its records. The three rows above list the pages of each piece.

report.md, finding F1

Where a decision lives

An open decision is a card on the Design page it changes. The answer bar on Overview gathers every open one into one reply line. Once answered, the card shows your answer in place.

Why no Discussion page

The version history is the discussion. Version 1 held the research, version 2 the first design, version 3 the design after your answers. Each opens from the version switcher.

WPL-D3

Which work gets a document

Answered

A question like "is this file still used?" is answered in chat, while a one-off investigation sits between that and a feature.

Trade-offs

O1 Every task

  • One shape and one viewer for everything you open
  • An investigation that turns into a build keeps its link and grows a Design group
  • Some documents are very small

O2 Code only

  • Small reports stay separate
  • Two kinds of page again
  • When a report turns into a build, the link changes

One link holds every version

Every publish keeps the link, and each version keeps a frozen copy of itself that opens from the version switcher.

A version means you have something new to see. Fixes republish under the same number.

The process, with each step's owner

The design goes back and forth with you until nothing is open, then it becomes an issue and the build lands in Verification.

  1. You ask.Any ask that starts a piece of work.
    you
  2. Firstmate gives it a task code, a document folder and a brief.The brief names the folder, the link once there is one, the version to write and the pages this worker owns.
    firstmate
  3. The worker writes the version: Overview, then Research or Design pages.It writes only the content. The skill builds the page, so the look is the same every time.
    doc worker
  4. A main-account worker publishes it at the same link.With the version label and the frozen copy.
    publisher
  5. Firstmate checks it, then sends "ready: link".The skill's check passes, and every answer you gave shows in the design.
    firstmate
  6. You answer in chatwith the copy line from Overview, or in your own words.
    you
  7. Firstmate records your answers and starts the next round.Code ledger and memory as today, your words into the brief, and the same worker writes the next version.
    firstmate
  8. When nothing is open, the Issue page is written and the issue filed.Half 2 starts.
    firstmate
  1. The builder builds and opens the PR.Kaspars' issue handoff or our own worker. The PR body links the issue and the document.
    builder
  2. A new version shows the PR in Verification and on Overview.CI state, changed screens before and after.
    doc updater
  3. The tester runs the document's checks on the PR head.The request names the check codes, so results come back per check.
    tester
  4. A new version shows the results.A failed check goes back to the builder, as today.
    doc updater
  5. Merge.Your word, or the standing rule where you gave one. The merge sign-off still applies.
    you
  6. The final version marks the work done.The document stays as the record.
    doc updater
WPL-D2

Where you answer

Answered

You read each decision on the Design page it changes, and your answer has to reach firstmate.

Trade-offs

O1 In chat

  • Same on laptop and phone
  • Firstmate records it the moment you send it
  • You switch from the page to chat

O2 On the page

  • You answer where you read
  • A store per document, and firstmate checking it
  • The 2 Oct prototype had this and it went unused

Your answer becomes the next version

Firstmate records your chat answer in three places, and no ready link goes out until the next version shows every answer.

The skill that builds every document

Workers write only the content, and the work-doc skill builds the page, so every document looks the same.

Moving to feedwrk-brain. The skill's home is feedwrk-brain, as a follow-up task. It builds on systems/docs from the design hub.

A document's folder

FileHoldsWritten by
doc.jsoncode, title, link, status, versionsdoc worker
content.htmlthe pages, one section eachdoc worker
index.htmlthe page to publishthe skill
v/1.html …frozen copies of earlier versionsthe skill

build.py check finds shape problems, build.py freeze writes the page and its frozen copy, and build.py sync takes a new Feedwrk Docs version.

Publishing a version

  1. Raise the version in doc.json and add its line.Date, what changed, what caused it.
    doc worker
  2. Write Overview's "What changed in version N", then the pages.Only the pages the brief names.
    doc worker
  3. Run check, then freeze.Check must print ok.
    doc worker
  4. Publish index.html at the document's link, with every v/N.html and the version label.A second-account worker stops here and a main-account Haiku publishes.
    publisher

WPL-D4

Work already under way

Answered

Your rule: all work under way is made to fit at its next move, so a piece at PR stage gets its original design document updated to status PR and presented.

Trade-offs

O1 Next move

  • No big migration, and links you have keep working
  • Older pages get a "Replaced by" note
  • For a while some pieces have documents and some do not

O2 All now

  • One cut-over
  • A large batch for pieces that are parked or nearly done

O3 New only

  • No migration
  • Home and Push stay scattered until they finish

The issue is where Design ends

When nothing is open, the last Design page becomes the issue, filed and linked both ways, standing alone for Kaspars' runs.

From the documentInto the issueHandoff check
OverviewFirst line: Document: <link> · version 4 · 22 Octnew: the link back
Design pagesWhat and why, the steps in build order, done-when per stepR1 R2
Design · Tables, ADRsEvery table, column, migration, API change and ADR, approved in version 4R4
VerificationHow each check runs, the verifier and its check codes, dataset name@versionR3 R9
Overview"Open decisions: none". Hand steps before and during the build. Existing branch or noneR5 R6 R7 R8

Linked both ways

The issue's first line links the document and its version. The Issue page links the issue and says whether it still matches. The PR body links both.

When the design changes after filing

Firstmate rewrites the affected issue sections and moves the first line to the new version. A running build is steered by one issue comment, as today.

WPL-D1

When the settled design becomes an issue

Answered

Once your answers leave nothing open in a version, someone files the issue from it.

Trade-offs

O1 Files it

  • No wait between your last answer and a buildable issue
  • It is on GitHub before you look at the final version

O2 Asks first

  • You read the final version before anything reaches GitHub
  • One more message per piece, and the work waits
WPL-D5

Kaspars and the documents

Answered

Documents are private claude.ai pages, and on 2 Oct Kaspars' run could not read the page linked from issue #243.

Trade-offs

O1 Private

  • Nothing leaves your account
  • Matches how his handoffs work today
  • Kaspars sees the build steps, not the research behind them

O2 Share

  • He sees the why and every version
  • Anyone with the link can read it, decisions and notes included
